snippet: for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) out[i] = parseInt(hex.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16);
reason: Equivalent: the extra iteration writes out[out.length], which is out of bounds on a Uint8Array and silently discarded; the decoded bytes are identical for every input.

Equivalent on every supported runtime: globalThis.crypto is present, so both conditions are true and both return the same globalThis.crypto.subtle; they differ only where crypto exists without subtle, which no runtime in the engines range has.

Equivalent at the API: only verify() can pass fromHex an odd-length or non-string value (sign() checks the key length first), and there the mutant either throws a different TypeError or decodes a short buffer that WebCrypto then rejects; both paths end in verify() returning false, as the tests check.
